fragment.response_text: {"paragraphs":[{"paragraph_id":"MA-S1:P1","paragraph_markdown":"Existing reranking architectures face a fundamental efficiency challenge when extending from single-passage scoring to cross-passage inference. In cross-passage inference, the model must attend across multiple retrieved passages simultaneously, so inference cost scales with the number of passages fed into the attention mechanism rather than remaining constant per passage. This scaling behavior makes cross-passage reranking substantially more expensive at inference time than listwise or pointwise alternatives that score each passage independently. The present setup addresses this by filtering candidate documents before they enter the reranking stage: a document is retained for downstream inference only when its size field is not None and its chunk identifier matches the corresponding query chunk identifier. This pre-filtering step reduces the passage set that the cross-passage attention layer must process, directly targeting the efficiency bottleneck without altering the inference architecture itself.","rendered_from_facet_ids":[],"rendered_slot_ids":[],"used_formula_package_ids":[],"witnesses":[]},{"paragraph_id":"MA-S1:P2","paragraph_markdown":"Beyond raw inference cost, cross-passage inference introduces a second challenge: the model must infer relevance signals that span passage boundaries, which single-passage scorers cannot capture. When passages are truncated or independently scored, contextual cues that appear only in the joint attention over multiple passages are lost, degrading ranking quality for queries whose answer is distributed across a passage neighborhood. The filtering condition described above—retaining a document only when its size is defined and its chunk identifier aligns with the query chunk—ensures that the passages reaching the cross-pattention stage are coherent fragments of the same logical unit, so that cross-passage attention operates on semantically contiguous content rather than on an arbitrary mixture. This design choice couples the retrieval filter with the inference objective: the filter selects passages that are jointly informative, and the cross-passage model exploits that joint structure to produce a more accurate relevance estimate than any per-passage score could achieve.","rendered_from_facet_ids":[],"rendered_slot_ids":[],"used_formula_package_ids":[],"witnesses":[]}],"section_id":"MA-S1"}
